title: Friedberg jump inversion

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; §20.2, Theorem 20.7 and full proof, p.81; fixed selector, coding/decoding programs and supplied reduction witnesses expanded

summary: Construct a weaker oracle whose jump has any prescribed degree above ordinary halting, with explicit coding and recovery.
abstract: Every oracle has a strictly harder halting problem. Can a given difficult membership problem be realized as the halting problem of some weaker oracle? Friedberg jump inversion answers yes whenever the given problem can already decide ordinary halting. We place its successive membership bits after finite extensions chosen to make the new oracle generic, so that the new oracle together with ordinary halting recovers exactly the original information. The generic jump identity then gives the desired inverse, even when finitely many initial bits of the new oracle are prescribed. This characterizes the range of the jump on Turing degrees, while noncomputable low sets show that an inverse degree need not be unique.
